title: Seven architectures, one engine
subtitle: Every facade here was written by an author who could not read the engine - only a brief, a schema, a facet list and two photographs of the mass. Each was given a different architecture to pursue and nothing else. All of them had to pass the design gates AND render before they counted, which is a stricter bar than this project used until today.

candidates.note: A bent-bar terrace bridge: the bar touches the ground at one entrance pier only, everything else cantilevers from z=1.861. 37 facets, widths 0.02 to 5.5 m.
A plain extruded prism: 35 vertices, two z levels, every vertical face a full rectangle, five storeys, sixteen facets. It sits on the ground and it does not step.

sections.title: Seven architectures
sections.note: Not material treatments of one building - different buildings. The engine, the two masses and the gates are identical across all of them; what differs is what the author was asked to make, and latterly what the grammar was able to say. One scheme is missing: an all-glass skin on the star prism cleared every design gate and every elevation and was rejected three times by the plan cut alone. Its author left the most useful result of that day - halving the depth of the members at the seam changed the seam by not one pixel.

cards.title: Level
cards.intent: Two constructions on a stepped bar: a unitised skin on the street, a brick wall carrying a precast order on the other three faces. Its spandrel course holds 3.3 and 6.6 across fourteen facets that begin at seven different heights, and the parapet ends the building on one line at 9.90. The crown is selected by asking whether a band's top edge is the building's own top slab - a question three earlier authors reported as unanswerable, because the facets that must crown are shorter than the facets that must not.

cards.title: Strata
cards.intent: The first facade written after an author could choose what a member is made of. A brick arcade at the ground, a precast frame above it, a metal attic under a metal cornice - the same terminals throughout, changing only in substance, with relief tracking material so the strata survive a grey render. Its author also named the limit: `wall` emits no geometry, so the field between the openings is the mass's own material at every height. You can trim a base in brick; you cannot yet make one of it.

cards.title: Arched masonry
cards.intent: Load-bearing wall where the arch is structural rather than ornamental - thick wall, deep reveal, openings that change as the load changes up the building.

cards.title: One great opening
cards.intent: The first scheme in this project with two constructions on one building: a unitised curtain wall on the street face, punched masonry behind it, and on the masonry one window 1.2 by 11.85 m - eleven times the area of anything beside it - cutting through four floors.

cards.title: Layered screen
cards.intent: Depth as the whole subject. Glass at 0, transom at 0.08, spandrel at 0.14, mullion at 0.18, fins at 0.32, cornice at 0.85 - a facade that is a section rather than a pattern. Its author found a contradiction in the brief getting here.

cards.title: Inverted weight
cards.intent: Open at the ground and denser as it rises, so the mass is carried above the street. The one scheme where the underside datum is live: a single level soffit line runs under a base that steps four times.

cards.title: Ribbon
cards.intent: Horizontal and nothing else - continuous bands of opening against continuous bands of solid, with no vertical member permitted to read, held level across a mass whose facets begin at seven different heights.

sections.title: The reversed loop
sections.note: One day, one mass, four languages - and the last one was designed by an image. crest2 answers the stepped mass with a level crown selected by the band's own edge; crest3 adds reach so the crown course meets its corner instead of pausing 0.3 m short; the colonnade is the first pier scheme through the plan gate since a member could say what it is made of; and imagefirst was transcribed by a vision author from a GPT-Image-2 concept - fin pitch, floor bands and the portal measured off the picture, the twist recorded as the loss the grammar cannot yet say.

cards.title: Crestline
cards.intent: A level crown over a terraced bar: every facet within one storey of the building top rises to 9.90, the steps stay legible in the punched body below.

cards.title: Crestline, cornered
cards.intent: The same design with reach: all 24 crown cornices run to their facet edges, so the cap reads as one course turning the building instead of 24 lintels.

cards.title: Colonnade
cards.intent: Chipperfield-language piers, 118 of them - the scheme the plan gate used to kill, rendered end to end under the material field.

cards.title: Image-first
cards.intent: Transcribed from a free GPT-Image-2 concept: 0.72 m fin modules over a glazed skin, a precast band reaching every facet edge at every floor, dark full-height slots, the fins written precast because the picture's fins are light metal.

cards.title: Image-first, graded
cards.intent: The same transcription with one added line - grade: depth_m 0.12 to 0.45 - so the 237 fins deepen along every glazing run and the screen reads as a field, not a stamp. The first scheme through the gates with the field-sampled attribute the parametric literature converged on.

sections.title: Three alternatives, one morning
sections.note: Opposed intents commissioned as alternatives after the image lane went down: a stone monolith, streamline horizontals, a Miesian bronze grid. All three accepted; the monolith passed attempt one, zero faults, and rendered clean end to end. The other two are the morning's real finding: both render all four elevations and are then blocked by gates whose measurements no longer respond to what an author can write - the bronze grid's right face pins at luminance P05 9.69 through three different grammars (the darkest pixels are the glass itself), and the streamline's two plan seams sit at the same coordinates through a controlled A/B on the member the diagnosis blamed. The gate files carry both measurements.

cards.title: Monolith
cards.intent: Excavated, not assembled: one substance, arches in four sizes cut into a thick wall, 0.5 m reveals carrying the shadow, the poorest face at 14.1% claimed as the closed-wall decision the intent demands.

cards.title: Streamline
cards.intent: Horizontals and nothing else: dark window bands against light metal decks reaching every corner, relief graded 0.14 to 0.30 up the storeys, hairline corner piers that vanish into the bands. Elevations accepted; the plan cut holds two grammar-invariant seams.

cards.title: Bronze grid
cards.intent: A strict 1.35 m Miesian module, sombre bronze on amber, precast spandrels holding the luminance range. Elevations accepted; the right face's darkest 5% is the glass, and no member edit moves it.

sections.title: The revival
sections.note: Six schemes the plan cut had killed, re-rendered untouched the day the seam detector stopped prosecuting the drawing's own ink. The seams were never in these designs: a thin member crossing the 1.2 m cut leaves two parallel ribbon strokes, and the pixel canyon between them measured as a same-material seam on one plane - eight hypotheses and one controlled A/B died on that canyon before a mesh probe at the failing pixels named it. Every card here is byte-identical to the grammar that was rejected.

cards.title: Flying curtain wall
cards.intent: Skin on all four faces of a lifted beam, a datum cornice at 9.90 and a soffit band at the underside line, neither a number in the file. Accepted 09-01 with the ledger note 'it does not render'; it renders.

cards.title: Soaring piers
cards.intent: Piers through three storeys - the vertical order the lockstep gate asks for, on the mass that kept killing piers at the cut.

cards.title: Arcade
cards.intent: Sixty-five arches - the Kahn language, first blind use of the arch terminal, dead at the plan since August.

cards.title: Sheer skin
cards.intent: The all-glass skin on the prism that cleared every design gate and every elevation and was rejected three times by the plan cut alone; its author's parting measurement - halving member depth changed the seam by not one pixel - was the first proof the seams were not theirs.

sections.title: Composed, not plumbed
sections.note: The afternoon the grammar stopped needing an engineer for every element. A split partitioned its scope exactly once, so two constructions could never share a rectangle and each composed element - a screen in front of glass, a balcony - had to arrive as new hand-written code. The layer axis hands every part the whole scope instead, stacked in depth, and these are the first designs to use it: the palazzo's balcony is a precast slab course and a baluster rail layered over the window bay behind, composed by its author out of words the grammar already had.

cards.title: Brick palazzo
cards.intent: Fifty-six brick piers, seventeen arches at the ground, deep reveals and a precast crown - the masonry language that could not render at all until the plan cut stopped prosecuting its own ink this morning.

cards.title: Palazzo with balconies
cards.intent: The same intent written after the layer axis existed: a 0.35 m slab course and eleven balusters standing in front of the window bay, and piers whose depth swells 0.5 to 0.35 toward the entrance. No new terminal was added for either move.

sections.title: Materials the author named
sections.blurb: Until today a facade could be made of four things, because the grammar had four words for material. These are the first buildings whose materials the architect DECLARED - a substance, a lightness, a hue, a finish and a module, under a name of their own - with the engine deriving the colour, the roughness, the metalness, the gate role and the joint module from those words. No hex codes were written by anyone.

cards.title: Zinc star tower
cards.intent: Transcribed from a freely generated perspective by an author told only that the massing was fixed and everything else was theirs. Five declared materials: ink-panel (pressed aluminium tray, powder-coated red iron oxide), bronze-surround, oak-reveal, warm-vision-glass and dark-coping. The author corrected its own coping mid-run - a folded zinc cap IS thin folded sheet, not solid metal - and refused a joint course I proposed to satisfy a gate, on the grounds that the render's joints are open joints and five projecting string courses per facet would draw lines the elevation does not have.

cards.title: Stone monolith
cards.intent: Five declared materials on the cleft block: fold-precast and core-cast (two concretes the author refused to merge), plinth-stone, slot-glass and reveal-bronze. It failed one render gate on one pair in one view - the bronze reveals and the stone plinth read as a single material on the elevation that faces away from the sun - and the author repaired it by changing a single word, mid-dark to mid, on the argument that a reveal is the darkest place on a building and a dark metal put there is not a material but the shadow it stands in. Role separation on that face 4.76 to 31.53, geometry untouched.
